doc: The match camera (CamRig, scripts/match/cam.gd). styles: the Settings 'Camera' presets: pitch in degrees down from level, dist m back from the focus, fov the vertical lens in degrees, rise m the view aims above the focus. hunter_scale: match Hunters are drawn that many times bigger (on top of Hunter.VIS_SCALE; hitboxes and hit circles keep their size), so the default view shows the source's ground across and its Hunter size together (docs/MOVEMENT_FEEL.md 'Source scale flag'); the home's own framing ignores it. supervive is that wide default (36.3 m back, 37 m across), supervive_close the older view (23 m). reach_ref_m: the camera distance the draw, LOD and shadow distances were tuned for (CamRig.reach scales them with the view). follow: the Settings 'Camera follow' cursor lean: [deadzone, share or maxzone, cap m, ease 1/s, quadratic easing]; supervive reads the cursor's distance from you in metres (deadzone m, share of the distance past it), the others its distance from the screen centre (-1..1). lean_edge_m: metres the cursor lean and an aimed cast keep between you and the screen's edge. source: the bands docs/MOVEMENT_FEEL.md 'Camera framing vs the source' measured from the source footage; --cam-framing-check holds the supervive style inside them; --move-feel-check holds its medium Hunter inside hunter_screen_pct.

trail.doc: The camera's follow across the ground [footage: briefs/hero-ref/dredge.md 4 and 8, ostra.md 2-3, mooshmoosh.md 2; 50 px = 1 m]. Each frame the view closes on you at min(follow_rate x gap, sqrt(2 x catch_decel x gap)) m/s: a run keeps it ~0.35 m behind and stopped with you in ~0.2 s, and a dash leaves it behind, then it eases in at a steady deceleration (Grimble's 4.6 m dash in 0.12 s: the pan peaks ~700 px/s, is down to ~300 px/s at 0.3 s and stops by ~0.5 s; ~0.4 s for a blink). follow_rate (1/s): the tight part, near you. catch_decel (m/s^2): fitted to that pan. max_gap (m): the furthest it may trail, just over the source dash's own ~3.2 m gap, so a long 40 m/s Wirerun can't take you off screen. cut_speed (m/s): a move faster than this in one frame is a teleport, and the view cuts to it, as the source does on Motley's Lantern Trade.

zoom.doc: How far in and out the view goes (CamWheel, scripts/match/cam_wheel.gd; the screens that show your hunter use ViewZoom). match: the mouse wheel in a match sets a zoom factor between min (closer: about the old 23 m view) and max (wider: 51 m back), step per notch; 1 is the style's own framing, and the player's setting is remembered (Settings cam_zoom). widen: what stretches the view on top of that, easing back when it ends: ctrl (sneak: hold Ctrl) and glide multiply it, and Ctrl always reaches at least ctrl_floor times max, so it goes past the wheel's range. The aimed-cast widening is its own number, Vex's Longneedle: content/archetypes/gunslinger.json e.view_zoom. preview: the hunter on the Relics, look-maker and results screens: wheel step per notch, pad_rate zoom per second at full stick, ease 1/s.
